newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel rises against dollar.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel rises against dollar.

text.p: The Israeli shekel gained mildly against the dollar but closed almost unchanged against the basket of foreign currencies following the dollar's weakening in Europe, dealers said.
"The shekel rose slightly against the dollar following the decline of the dollar abroad. Outherwise, nothing happened in the market and activity was very low," a dealer at Israel Discount Bank said.

"Just before the end of the trading day the Bank of Israel started buying dollars on a very low scale and the representative rate of the basket was set at exactly seven percent below the slope," he said.

The shekel can trade in a band of seven percent above or below a slope designed to devalue the Israeli currency at six percent a year against a basket of currencies representing Israel's main trading partners.

The representative rate for the dollar was 3.1880 against 3.1910 on Monday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, closed at 3.5609 shekels against 3.5611 on Monday.
On the crosses the shekel traded against the yen at 2.8674 shekels per 100 yen against 2.8636 on Monday and against the mark at 2.0896 shekels per mark against 2.0847 on Monday.
In late afternoon the dollar was trading at 3.1870 shekels.
